title: Client-side yield (until=stack_resolved) cancels pending GAME_TARGET, causing spell-cancel loops
description:
When a model casts a spell that requires targets (e.g. Flames of the Firebrand) and then calls pass_priority(until="stack_resolved") or get_action_choices(until="stack_resolved"), the bridge unconditionally sends sendPlayerBoolean(gameId, false) at BridgeCallbackHandler.java:3043-3046. This cancels the pending GAME_TARGET action, the spell fizzles, and the card returns to hand. The model then tries to cast the same spell again, entering a loop that wastes 3-7 minutes per turn until the loop detector fires.

The bug is that lines 3043-3046 don't check pendingAction.method() before sending false. For step-phase until values (precombat_main, etc.), the code correctly enters the main loop where the method != GAME_SELECT guard at line 3167 catches non-priority actions and returns them to the model. But for client-side yields (stack_resolved, end_of_turn, my_turn), the code bypasses the loop entirely.

Evidence from game_20260228_172012_g2:
- GPT52 Philo tried to cast Flames of the Firebrand 9 times across turns 8, 10, and 16, each time the targeting was auto-cancelled
- Chandra, Heart of Fire (+1: deal 2 damage) activation was attempted ~8 times across turns 12 and 14, each time cancelled
- Chandra was on the board for 19 minutes without a single successful activation
- The loop detector fired 5 times on GPT52 Philo's turns
- GPT52 Philo made 268 tool calls vs Opus Teach's 121, with 2639s thinking time vs 592s

Suggested fix: Before lines 3043-3046, check if pendingAction is a non-priority action (GAME_TARGET, GAME_ASK, GAME_CHOOSE_ABILITY, GAME_CHOOSE_CHOICE, GAME_PLAY_MANA). If so, return the pending action's choices with stop_reason="non_priority_action" instead of cancelling. This matches the behavior already implemented in the main loop at line 3167.

Source: BridgeCallbackHandler.java:3043-3046
